data.name: rag-web-browser
data.description: Web search and fetch tool for AI agents and RAG pipelines. It queries Google Search, scrapes the top N pages using a full web browser, and returns their content as clean Markdown for further processing by an LLM. Can also fetch individual URLs.

sourceFiles.content:
# First, specify the base Docker image. You can read more about
# the available images at https://sdk.apify.com/docs/guides/docker-images
# You can also use any other image from Docker Hub.
FROM apify/actor-node:16

# Second, copy just package.json and package-lock.json since those are the only
# files that affect "npm install" in the next step, to speed up the build.
COPY package*.json ./

# Install NPM packages, skip optional and development dependencies to
# keep the image small. Avoid logging too much and print the dependency
# tree for debugging
RUN npm --quiet set progress=false \
 && npm install --only=prod --no-optional \
 && echo "Installed NPM packages:" \
 && (npm list || true) \
 && echo "Node.js version:" \
 && node --version \
 && echo "NPM version:" \
 && npm --version

# Next, copy the remaining files and directories with the source code.
# Since we do this after NPM install, quick build will be really fast
# for most source file changes.
COPY . ./

# Optionally, specify how to launch the source code of your Actor.
# By default, Apify's base Docker images define the CMD instruction
# that runs the Node.js source code using the command specified
# in the "scripts.start" section of the package.json file.
# In short, the instruction looks something like this:
#
# CMD npm start

data.readmeSummary:
## RAG Web Browser

A web-browsing and web-scraping Actor designed to provide up-to-date web context for LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines: it issues web searches, crawls top search results or specific URLs, renders JavaScript when needed with a headless browser, expands collapsed page sections, extracts page metadata (title, description, language, canonical/OpenGraph data), converts HTML to clean Markdown/plain text/HTML, and returns ordered, de-duplicated absolute links with visible link text and crawl/status/timing information; it also supports a lightweight HTTP-fetch mode for static pages, media skipping, anti-scraping bypass via proxies and browser fingerprints, and integration via OpenAPI/MCP for function-calling and low-latency HTTP server deployments for parallel requests.

## Use cases

- Feed LLM applications and RAG pipelines with up-to-date web content discovered via web search.  
- Crawl and extract content from specific web pages (including JavaScript-rendered pages) and convert it to Markdown or plain text for prompt context.  
- Provide search-driven collections of top results (titles, descriptions, page metadata, and extracted content) for semantic retrieval.  
- Integrate web browsing capabilities into custom AI assistants, GPTs, and MCP-based agent workflows via OpenAPI/function-calling.  
- Low-latency, production-ready web extraction using a standby HTTP server that handles parallel requests.  
- Fast static-site scraping using a lightweight HTTP fetch mode when JavaScript rendering is not required.  
- Extract and normalize links on pages into absolute URLs with associated visible text for downstream citation or navigation.  
- Capture content hidden in collapsed elements (accordions/FAQ) by expanding them before extraction.  
- Avoid downloading media files during scraping to focus on textual content for LLM consumption.
